description: Implements your interface on top of a foreign API, translating inputs, outputs, units and errors so the vendor never leaks into your code.
Wraps an object with the same interface and adds behavior (logging, limits, retries, caching) before or after delegating.
A function that decides which implementation to build (and how to wrap it) from configuration, usually at startup.
The outermost wrapper runs first. Logging outside a limit sees rejected calls; logging inside sees only allowed ones.
Throw on invalid configuration at startup instead of silently falling back to a default implementation.
Hexagonal architecture: the core defines interfaces (ports); infrastructure plugs in through adapters.
